> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0819cab13c33b6b996c0a5c410052d9524fcf1f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4f20e3df7cb847423b36c474e18e6a11a40b18c5` — the merge of head `ffdb13cd4eb7951637870fba588d258e611ca578` into base `0819cab13c33b6b996c0a5c410052d9524fcf1f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4f20e3df7cb847423b36c474e18e6a11a40b18c5 && git checkout 4f20e3df7cb847423b36c474e18e6a11a40b18c5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0819cab13c33b6b996c0a5c410052d9524fcf1f7 ffdb13cd4eb7951637870fba588d258e611ca578 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0819cab13c33b6b996c0a5c410052d9524fcf1f7 && git merge --no-ff ffdb13cd4eb7951637870fba588d258e611ca578

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0819cab13c33b6b996c0a5c410052d9524fcf1f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0819cab13c33b6b996c0a5c410052d9524fcf1f7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head ffdb13cd · 2026-11-24T07:00Z

L1 read of #36878 against card #36410, item 1 only (`Refs`; item 2, the `NavigationOverlay` slot, stays on the card for the seat). Seat route A, claim amendment 7120223249, carrier-file note 7124480262. Head `ffdb13cd4eb7951637870fba588d258e611ca578`; dev report 7124457469.

**Face.** `l1-face.mjs --pr 36878` CLEAN (13 items read, none flagged). At this head: 55 checks succeed, 10 skip as expected, 0 fail. `mergeable_state` clean. `check-governed-merges.mjs` says NOT governed. `Clause-②: no`: `actionUrl` keeps its string shape and its "only pointer" role. `Metadata-protocol: none`.

**Producer (`plugin-audit` `audit-writers.ts`), read and sound.**
- `commentRecordPath` builds `/{object}/{id}?comments={rootId}`, adding `&comment={commentId}` only when the comment is not the root. With no root it returns the record alone, and with no record it returns `null`, so no `url` is set.
- A top-level mention is its own thread. A mention in a reply walks up through the factored `walkToThreadRoot` (bounded, cycle-safe, held to the thread). A failed walk is logged and falls back to the record link. A reply notice reuses `readThreadParticipants`' walk, which now also returns `rootId`, so it costs no extra read.
- The e-mail `mentionUrl` and reply URL are the same path made absolute through `getConsoleUrl`. The recipient gate (read both the record and the comment) is unchanged.
- `actionUrlFor`, the spec and stored rows are untouched (no backfill), all as the route says.

**Console, read and sound.**
- Desktop: `RecordDetailView` opens the panel when `?comments={thread}` is present, without writing the stored open or closed choice. Closing a panel the link opened drops both params with a replace, so it stays closed. `openCommentsPage` and `leaveCommentsPage` drop `comment` whenever the reader moves on.
- Phone: the existing `?comments=` page receives `focusCommentId`.
- `CommentsPanel` with `focusThreadId` / `focusCommentId`:
  - It widens the filter to show all, once, when the linked thread is hidden.
  - It opens the thread's replies (`openSignal`) and marks the target.
  - It scrolls the list (never the page) to it once, then hands scrolling back to the reader. The foot-follow resumes only after a thread is added.
  - A stale link (thread not present) leaves the list at its foot.
- `RECORD_COMMENT_PARAM` is reserved in `RESERVED_URL_PARAMS`.

**Tests.** I count 7 test files changed across the producer and console. The producer integration pins cover the reply notice, the mention e-mail and the recipient gate with the new link. The console pins use the real `RecordDetailView` (desktop open via link, closing drops the params, the stored choice unchanged), `CommentsPanel` (hidden thread shown, replies opened, target marked, stale link) and `CommentsPage`. Ablations 1-5 each go red.

**Changeset, read sentence by sentence.** Every sentence matches the diff. Leaving out the private `@object-ui/app-shell` is correct.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Notes (nit, no action required):
- N1. The declared deviations are accepted. `urlParams.ts` (reserves `comment`) and `recordCommentsPanel.tsx` (pass-through) sit outside the amended fence, but they are mechanical, in a private package, and recorded on the card (7124480262). The overlap-check ran just after a push, and the full local app-shell suite was stopped with CI Test UI green.
- N2. Browser reach was NOT MEASURED. jsdom does no layout, so `scrollCommentIntoView`'s geometry (centring the comment, scrolling only the list) is unproven by the pins, which prove only that it finds the comment and is called. The card's acceptance ("shows that comment without another click") is visual. One browser check at landing would settle it: a notice for a reply deep in a long, resolved thread.
- N3. A mention in a reply now costs one bounded `parent_id` walk per mention write. That is fine at comment volume, and noted for anyone who later batches mention emits.
